reason: In Judges 15, the men of Judah (described as 'three thousand men' - regular people/militia) demonstrate clear antagonism toward Samson, their leader/judge. They come to bind him and plan to deliver him to the Philistines, saying 'Why have you come up against us?' and 'What have you done to us?' They explicitly state their intention to bind Samson and hand him over to the Philistines as retribution for his actions against them. Samson himself recognizes the threat, asking them to swear they won't kill him themselves. This represents direct antagonism from the populace against their leader due to consequences of his actions.
